messages.text: My miner arrived faulty

I'm Hal, HeliumDeploy's technical specialist. I'm sorry it arrived faulty. Let's work out what's going on.

I can see two orders on your email, Shop···· (placed Oct 19) and Shop···· (placed Sep 21). To start:

1. Which miner is it, and which order did it come on?
2. What does it do when you plug it in? For example: no power at all, fans spin but no screen, the screen shows an error, or it powers on but won't hash.

A photo of the screen or the unit would help a lot if you can send one.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)
Searched the web · AxeOS "VOLTAGE PROTECTION" "Guru Meditation" G0008000
Used the heliumdeploy-ops-knowledge skill
Searched the web · NerdQaxe "Guru Meditation" voltage protection error
I'll check the exact code in the firmware source.
Searched the web · shufps ESP-Miner-NerdQAxePlus "Voltage Protection" guru medi
Read github.com/shufps/ESP-Miner-NerdQAxePlus/issues/755

Thanks for the photo. Here's what your screen shows:

- A red **"VOLTAGE PROTECTION, Guru Meditation #····"** error
- 0.0 GH/s, 0.062 W, 33 °C, BM1370 chips
- Wi-Fi is connected and the miner's IP is 192.168.4.68

So the miner boots and joins your network, but it has cut power to the chips. It's running cool, so heat isn't the cause.

I won't guess what that exact code means. I tried to look it up in the maker's firmware source and couldn't confirm it yet. Different firmware versions use these codes differently, so I need two things from you:

1. **Model and firmware version.** Open http://192.168.4.68 in a browser on the same Wi-Fi. The model and firmware version are on the main or System page. A screenshot is perfect.
2. **Power supply.** Are you using the power brick that came in the box, or a different one? If it has a label, what does it say for volts and amps?

Once I have those, I'll give you the next step.

Okay so I have done all the trouble shooting and its not the power supply you sent with it.  Its the board.  The firmware is the latest.  This is the order Shop····.  This will need an RMA.  It probably got damaged in shipping because the box came with no tape and the lid was partially opened and the top foam padding was missing along with any documentation that was in the box.
Used rma verdict

Thanks, that helps. What you're describing, with the miner joining Wi-Fi but cutting voltage to the chips and drawing almost no power, does point at the board rather than settings. I agree the packaging you describe is worth recording too.

To finish my technical check for Shop····, please send these:

1. **A short video** (10 to 20 seconds) of the miner from plugging it in until the VOLTAGE PROTECTION error appears.
2. **A clear photo of the serial number** sticker on the board.
3. **A screenshot of the firmware version** from http://192.168.4.68 (the main or System page). That also confirms the exact model.
4. **Photos of the box** as it arrived: the open lid, the missing tape and where the top foam should have been.
5. **One yes or no:** have you tried a second power supply other than the one in the box? If so, what are its volts and amps?

Once I have these, I'll finish my findings and pass them on.
I can't upload a video

Hal here, and no problem, the video is optional. Photos will do.

Please send what you can of these:

1. **The serial number sticker** on the board.
2. **The firmware version screen** from http://192.168.4.68 (a screenshot or a phone photo of your monitor is fine).
3. **The box** as it arrived, showing the open lid and the missing tape and foam.
4. **Yes or no:** have you tried a power supply other than the one in the box?

If you'd still like to show the video, you can paste a share link in the chat instead, for example from Google Drive or an unlisted YouTube upload. You don't have to, though.
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Got it, thanks. The photo shows the brown BSB box with no tape on it, and the end flap on the right side is folded out instead of tucked in. That matches what you described.

Next, please send:

1. **A photo inside the box**, showing where the top foam should be.
2. **The serial number sticker** on the board.
3. **The firmware version screen** from http://192.168.4.68.
4. **Yes or no:** have you tried a power supply other than the one in the box?
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)
Read github.com/shufps/ESP-Miner-NerdQAxePlus/releases
Searched the web · NerdQAxePlus firmware release v1.1.2

Thanks. Your screenshot shows a **NerdQAxe++ (BM1370) on firmware v1.1.2**, with Wi-Fi connected at a strong -49 dBm and "Power on reset" as the last reset reason.

v1.1.2 looks like the newest release on the maker's GitHub. 
A v1.1.2-alpha.1 test build came out on 7 Nov
, followed by the v1.1.2 release itself, so firmware is ruled out.

The logs will tell us more than a video would. Please:

1. On that page, click **SHOW LOGS**.
2. Click **RESTART** and let it run until the VOLTAGE PROTECTION error appears.
3. Send a photo or screenshot of the log lines from just before the error. The useful lines mention "ASIC voltage", "VR", "TPS" or "voltage".

If you can, please also send the **serial number sticker** photo and answer yes or no: **have you tried a power supply other than the one in the box?**
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Thanks. This one shows the open box from above:

- The dark grey bottom foam insert with its cut-outs, now empty since the miner is out.
- No top foam layer over it.
- A small silver bag in the left cut-out with something yellow inside.
- A white card standing on the right side that looks like a quick start card.

I've noted all of it, along with the box photo from before.

That leaves three things to finish my check:

1. **Logs:** click SHOW LOGS, then RESTART, and photograph the lines just before the VOLTAGE PROTECTION error.
2. **Serial number sticker** on the board.
3. **Yes or no:** have you tried a power supply other than the one in the box?
(The customer sent this photo without a message.)

Got it, thanks. The sticker reads **Model: NerdQaxe++ 6T, Power Input: 12V XT30**. The serial under the barcode is a bit blurry, but it starts KY0126 and ends in 048, which is enough to go on.

The part of the board in this photo looks clean. I can see no burn marks or lifted parts around the cap····banks or the heatsink.

Two things left, then I can finish my check:

1. **Logs:** in the web page, click SHOW LOGS, then RESTART, and photograph the lines just before the VOLTAGE PROTECTION error.
2. **Yes or no:** have you tried a power supply other than the one in the box?
I do not have a PSU that is the same as this one so no

No problem, thanks for confirming.

The logs are the key piece now. "Voltage protection" can mean one of two things:

- **The power brick isn't delivering a steady 12 V.** That's a power supply problem, not the board.
- **The board's voltage regulator is faulty.** That's a board problem.

The log lines show which one it is. Please:

1. Open http://192.168.4.68 and click **SHOW LOGS**.
2. Click **RESTART** and wait for the VOLTAGE PROTECTION error.
3. Send a photo of the log lines just before the error, especially any that mention "voltage", "VR", "TPS" or "input".

Also, if you can, send a photo of the label on the power brick showing its volts and amps.
I do not want to keep this plugged in any longer since its having voltage issues and may trip a breaker.  Please just get me a human and lets get the RMA going.
Used rma verdict
Handed to the team · Customer asked for a human. Hal verdict is inconclusive: PSU vs board (TPS) is n

Understood, and keeping it unplugged is completely fine. For what it's worth, the screen showed it drawing only 0.062 W, so it was very unlikely to trip a breaker. Still, there's no need to power it again.

I've passed everything to the team with your request for a person:

- The VOLTAGE PROTECTION error screen
- Model NerdQaxe++ 6T and firmware v1.1.2, which is the current release
- The serial label
- Your photos of the untaped box and the missing top foam
- That only the power brick from the box has been tried

Someone will pick up your ticket and get back to you by email, usually within one business day.

If you're on Discord, you can also post there in the meantime: https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and mention @nullhashrate, our hardware lead.
